arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Gannon argued that Congress understood obstruction to include pre-proceeding crimes. He stated that the term covered acts before a formal case began. He emphasized the historical understanding of the phrase in 1996.
Ms. Hutton argued that the term implies interference with a pending proceeding. She stated that Congress chose a specific term of art. She emphasized the need for a nexus to an active legal process.

Justice Sotomayor asked about crimes that do not involve aiding a criminal. She questioned if failing to report a crime counts as obstruction. She sought to clarify the boundary of the legal definition.
Justice Kagan asked about the requirement of a nexus to a proceeding. She inquired if reasonable foreseeability is the standard. She referenced previous Board indications on this issue.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of a 1996 immigration statute. The law treats certain obstruction crimes as aggravated felonies. The core issue is the meaning of the phrase relating to obstruction of justice. One side argues the phrase covers crimes committed before a formal proceeding begins. The other side argues the phrase requires interference with an active legal process.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The government wants the Court to define obstruction broadly. It seeks to include crimes committed before a formal proceeding starts. This interpretation would allow deportation for a wider range of conduct.

the side that brought the case wants the Court to define obstruction narrowly. It seeks to limit the term to interference with a pending proceeding. This interpretation would exclude crimes committed before an investigation formally begins.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The government argues that Congress used a broad term of art. It contends that obstruction includes acts that hinder any future investigation. This view relies on the phrase relating to as a broadening modifier.

the side that brought the case argues that obstruction requires a specific nexus to an active process. It contends that the term implies interference with a pending proceeding. This view relies on the need for a reasonable foreseeability of a specific legal action.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Chief Justice Roberts asked how the phrase relating to affects the definition. He noted that a broad definition becomes even broader with this language. He questioned the scope of the term obstruction of justice.
Justice Thomas asked for a straightforward definition of obstruction of justice. He sought a clear boundary for the legal term. He wanted to understand the core meaning of the offense.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The definition of obstruction determines who faces deportation. A broad definition includes more criminal acts. A narrow definition excludes acts without a pending proceeding. This distinction affects the rights of non-citizens. It shapes the scope of federal immigration power. The outcome defines the boundary of criminal liability in this context.
